subject: maths

chapters.title: What's in a Name?
covers: Follows a story about herders who make a mark for each cow leaving and strike one off for each cow returning
Uses tally marks to keep track of 36 cows and 23 sheep
Works out how many cows came home when the marks left on the wall show the rest
Tries different ways to count a big group without using numbers, such as the children entering a classroom

chapters.title: Toy Joy
topics: making models from boxes and bottles
covers: Names the shapes of boxes, bottles and cones used to make animal and bird faces
Counts how many of each solid shape a toy rocket or engine uses
Says which faces are flat and which are curved, and which edges are straight
Builds houses, towers or rockets from shape objects and describes how they are arranged
Learns that a cube is a special kind of cuboid

chapters.title: Double Century
topics: how number symbols came to be
numbers up to 200 on a snakes-and-ladders board
covers: Estimates and then counts oranges, bangles, laddoos and other things in a picture
Fills in missing numbers on a board that goes up to 100
Plays a game with numbers that add up to 100, such as 70 and 30
Makes 100 by jumping along a number line in different ways
Works out what number comes one more or one less than a given number

chapters.title: Vacation with My Nani Maa
topics: a number trick with hidden seeds
covers: Finds the number hidden under a cloth by thinking of the number that makes 9, 10 or 20
Adds two groups of sweets, such as 7 and 5, and then finds the amount left after taking some away
Uses a tens frame to add and subtract, for example 6 + 8
Plays a card game where three cards that form a sum or difference are kept
Adds the number of books children collected for a grandmother

chapters.title: Fun with Shapes
covers: Copies a rangoli made on dots and names the shapes in it
Counts how many shapes in a rangoli are made with curved lines and how many with straight lines
Makes a rangoli design from objects found in the classroom
Looks at flattened boxes to find the 2D shapes that make up a solid
Folds a square of paper to make an envelope

chapters.title: House of Hundreds – I
covers: Counts torans and bangles in a mela, using hundreds, tens and ones
Counts toffees in boxes from 200 to 300 and sees that 299 plus one is 300
Works out how many more torans are needed to reach 300
Fills in missing numbers on a number track going past 200
Adds or subtracts 1, 10 or 20 from a given number, then writes the change in words

chapters.title: Raksha Bandhan
covers: Counts leaves, glasses, pomegranates and flowers in a decorated home
Works out how many threads, flowers and beads are needed for 5 rakhis
Writes equal additions such as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 as 5 times 2
Learns that 5 times 4 means 5 groups of 4 beads
Makes a rakhi at home

chapters.title: Fair Share
topics: checking that two parts are equal
covers: Decides whether a paratha or chocolate has been shared equally
Folds a rectangle or square of paper to find different ways to make a half
Shades the shapes where half of the whole is coloured
Shares mangoes equally between two children
Discusses whether a set of shared things, such as a tree and fruit, is fair

chapters.title: House of Hundreds – II
topics: hundreds, tens and ones with tiles
locating numbers on a number line
covers: Shows numbers such as 832 and 504 with hundred, ten and one tiles
Finds the number of sacks of rice by counting in hundreds, tens and ones
Locates numbers such as 530, 590 and 703 on a number line between 500 and 900
Makes a guess about the number of crows or students and checks it by counting
Reads a story about estimating a count of crows and what the guesses mean

chapters.title: Fun at Class Party!
covers: Finds the height of a door with informal units such as a hand span or a paper string
Compares a table measured by two children with different hand spans and asks why they differ
Picks the longest and the shortest strings in a picture
Measures the distance between two walls and thinks of other ways to measure it
Discusses which way of measuring length is better and why

chapters.title: Filling and Lifting
topics: litre, half litre and quarter litre
covers: Works out whether six big glasses of juice would be as many as six small ones
Pours milk from different glasses into same-sized glasses to see who drank the most
Guesses how many small bowls fill a glass or bottle, then checks by pouring
Decides whether a vessel holds more or less than one litre using a 1 litre measure
Matches vessels to a litre, half litre or quarter litre

chapters.title: Give and Take
topics: combining ten tens into a hundred
covers: Adds 364 and 52 saplings using a box diagram, grouping ones, tens and hundreds
Works out 230 minus 75 by taking away ones first, then tens
Changes 1 hundred into 10 tens when there are not enough tens to take away
Checks answers using a number line with jumps of 10
Solves word problems about saplings sold or packed in a nursery

chapters.title: Time Goes On
covers: Builds a full calendar for July by writing the dates under each weekday
Counts how many Sundays a month has and lists the Thursdays
Finds the date and weekday three days after a given date
Works out the reopening date after a 15-day school closure

chapters.title: The Surajkund Fair
topics: symmetry: a line dividing a shape into equal halves
covers: Spots things at a fair that look the same on the left and right
Folds a traced rangoli to see whether its two halves match
Draws the lines of symmetry in rangoli designs
Makes malas with 8 beads, 4 of each colour, and colours which are symmetrical
Looks around for other symmetrical objects

gaps: Chapter 11: the 'Lifting' half of the title is not described; the text read covered capacity only.
